topStory.headline: University of Huddersfield Launches Cross-Disciplinary A.I. Institute
topStory.summary:
The University of Huddersfield has launched the Institute for Applied Artificial Intelligence, the institution's first fully cross-disciplinary research center, according to the university. Professor John Murray leads the institute, which brings together faculty from computing, engineering, health, business, sciences, education, and the arts, along with professional staff.

The center focuses on responsible A.I. development and deployment to improve workplace efficiency. The institute includes two humanoid robots named Harold and Skye for assisted living research. The launch aligns with the UK government's Industrial Strategy, which identifies A.I. as a frontier industry in the digital technologies sector.

Unlike A.I. programs that remain siloed within computer science departments, Huddersfield's approach deliberately includes humanities and social sciences faculty. The Pro Vice-Chancellor for Teaching and Learning leads the institute, signaling that Huddersfield views A.I. integration as connected to pedagogy and student learning. The institute is recruiting two research fellows and requires specialized facilities for its cross-disciplinary work.

stories.headline: Maryville College Plans Second Annual A.I. Summit
stories.summary: Maryville College will host its second annual A.I. Summit on May 12-13, expanding beyond education to include business, nonprofit, and community perspectives, according to Knox TN Today. The event accepts session proposals until March 18 and emphasizes liberal arts approaches to A.I.'s ethical and social implications.

stories.headline: Cedarville Professor Uses Space Debris Research for A.I. Education
stories.summary: Dr. George Landon at Cedarville University applies his Air Force Academy space surveillance research to teach students about A.I.'s real-world limitations, according to Cedarville University. His approach shows students how A.I. models often fail with noisy data, fostering skepticism alongside practical skills.

stories.headline: Writing Professor Advocates Teaching Students When to Struggle
stories.summary: A Babson College writing professor describes shifting from neutral A.I. observer to active guide, helping students understand when A.I. shortcuts undermine learning, according to Economic Times Education. The approach involves comparing A.I.-assisted and unassisted work to develop student discernment about tool usage.
